subject.title: [Feature]: Support arbitrary workspace files in bootstrap context injection

question: Should OpenClaw accept explicitly configured custom-basename bootstrap files as a core hook contract, and should that include the exact-session sessions[sessionKey] shape from the linked PR?
rationale: The source limitation is clear, but accepting the fix changes deterministic system-prompt context and the automatic workspace file-loading contract rather than repairing a settled documented bug behavior.

options.title: Approve guarded custom files
options.body: Allow configured custom basenames through the existing hook path after the linked PR or replacement proves containment, budgets, ordering, and session filtering.

options.title: Narrow to global paths only
options.body: Accept arbitrary basenames for existing paths/patterns/files while deferring session-scoped selectors to a separate design item.

options.title: Keep recognized basenames
options.body: Retain the current allowlist and route custom-context needs to first-class workspace filename or broader context API proposals.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded custom files
recommendation.body: Allow configured custom basenames through the existing hook path after the linked PR or replacement proves containment, budgets, ordering, and session filtering.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original hook feature and authored adjacent boundary-safe workspace read refactoring, making him the strongest available routing candidate for the product/security boundary decision.
